observations.explanation: Page 5 reports CodeAct as best on success rate for 12 of 17 models and on average turns for 12 of 17. It also highlights GPT-4-1106-preview’s 20.7 percentage-point success improvement and 2.1 fewer turns.

Page 9 reports both CodeActAgent variants outperforming evaluated open-source models on MINT’s in-domain and out-of-domain subsets. The table on page 8 also shows gains on several tested general tasks, with results varying by baseline and task.

Page 5 describes M3ToolEval as 82 human-curated instances across several domains. The claim that this modest curated set limits how broadly its results establish real-world generality is a reasonable, appropriately scoped inference.

Page 10 identifies hallucination as a limitation and says future work should design better safety mechanisms for code execution in a sandbox. The reported evaluations do not establish that these concerns are resolved.
